 Titusville Police Investigation Leads to Arrest of Louis Grayson, 49, of Mims, After Major Drug Seizure
 By Space Coast Daily  //  November 8, 2026 
 TPD: Louis Grayson, 49, is being held at Brevard County Jail on a $258,500 bond 
 The Titusville police officers seized significant quantities of cocaine, fentanyl, multiple firearms, and materials associated with illegal drug distribution following a traffic stop and subsequent residential search warrant. A Titusville police spokesperson said the investigation began after TPD officers received multiple tips regarding suspected drug sales involving an individual identified as Louis Grayson, 49, of Mims. 
 TPD investigators recovered more than 150 grams of cocaine, five firearms, including four handguns and one rifle, and materials associated with illegal drug sales and manufacturing 
 BREVARD COUNTY • TITUSVILLE, FLORIDA – The Titusville police officers seized significant quantities of cocaine, fentanyl, multiple firearms, and materials associated with illegal drug distribution following a traffic stop and subsequent residential search warrant .
 A Titusville police spokesperson said the investigation began after TPD officers received multiple tips regarding suspected drug sales involving an individual identified as Louis Grayson, 49, of Mims.
 During surveillance, investigators observed Grayson traveling to a residence located in the 2500 block of Christopher Drive in Titusville.
 Grayson was seen entering the residence and then exiting with a clear bag containing suspected illegal narcotics.
 TPD officers conducted a traffic stop on the vehicle Grayson was driving for a window tint violation. During the stop, officers observed a piece of crack cocaine on his lap and a crack pipe on the seat.
 A search revealed approximately 56.7 grams of cocaine on Grayson’s person and an additional 28.8 grams of fentanyl inside the vehicle.
 TPD officers arrested him and transported him to the Brevard County Jail, where he is being held on a $258,500 bond.
 Grayson’s charges include: 
 • 1 count of trafficking fentanyl
• 1 count of trafficking cocaine
• 1 count of possession of crack cocaine
• 1 count of possession of drug paraphernalia
• 1 count of possession of a controlled substance while in physical control of a motor vehicle
 As the investigation progressed, detectives obtained and executed a search warrant at the residence Grayson visited on Christopher Drive.
 During the search, TPD investigators recovered: 
 • More than 150 grams of cocaine
• Five firearms, including four handguns and one rifle
• Materials associated with illegal drug sales and manufacturing
 “The Titusville Police Department remains committed to aggressively investigating illegal drug trafficking, removing dangerous narcotics and unlawfully possessed firearms from our community, and holding those responsible accountable,” said Titusville Police Chief Tyler “TJ” Wright. 
 “The Titusville Police Department remains committed to aggressively investigating illegal drug trafficking, removing dangerous narcotics and unlawfully possessed firearms from our community, and holding those responsible accountable,” said Titusville Police Chief Tyler “TJ” Wright.
 “Through proactive enforcement, thorough investigations, and valuable information provided by our community, we will continue working hard to disrupt criminal activity and protect the safety and well-being of our residents.”
 Titusville police detectives are actively investigating the occupants of the residence and their potential involvement in illegal narcotics activity.
 This remains an active investigation, and additional arrests or charges may follow as detectives continue their investigative efforts.
